source: Monnier et al. (2012), Resolving Vega and the Inclination Controversy with CHARA/MIRC, ApJL 761, L3 (https://arxiv.org/abs/1211.6055), Table 2, Model 3 "Concordance", read from the authors' LaTeX source
caption: Modeling Results for Vega. The Concordance Model incorporated the observed v sin i = 22 ± 2 km/s and the period estimate 0.71 ± 0.03 days as priors. Surface temperature follows T = T_pole (g/g_pole)^β.
note: Vega is seen almost pole-on, so its bright pole faces us. The paper warns that the pole position angle is fragile: fits to different epochs differ by as much as 90°. The Roche shape equation is not printed; the one used here reproduces the table's equatorial radius, equatorial temperature and surface-mean temperature (9360 ± 90 K) from its polar values, ω and β (tests).
